about: What the full system testnet contains and every stand-in it uses. It is deployed fresh on a local chain at every run, so no address is fixed here: ./dev demo buyback and ./dev demo full each print the addresses of their run and write them to .cache/demo/run/addresses.json. Both read the chain, LPT and pool values below from this file, and check the buyback values below against those Parameters holds at deployment, so what runs is what this file says. Rewards's testnet, rewards-local.json, still runs with ./dev demo.

contracts.checks: only the executor Parameters' group 10 names for the round a draw runs in may draw the network share (drawNetwork); at deployment that is the Buyback

contracts.node_name: none: Parameters names it as the deployment's score source, and Claims reads it as its validator set
none: the Broker reads its fee split from it, Claims, StakeLedger and Scores their values, and the Buyback its values (groups 8 and 9), and the Broker the executor that may draw (group 10)
contracts.checks: authority() is G, the governance stand-in; deployed after the TestPool, at the address the Broker, StakeLedger and Scores were given; its deployment buyback values are the TestPool and the buyback values below, and its deployment executor (group 10) is the Buyback, taken at construction as the address predicted for it
broker() is the Broker, values() is Parameters, poolCodeHash() is the runtime code hash of the TestPool deployed with it, and acceptsPool(TestPool) is true

node.changes: none: the unmodified node, configured by flags alone

price.ticket_face: the job price in micro-USDC plus 1: one ticket of 1 USDC a job

pool.note: Seeded by the deployer from its genesis LPT and freshly minted mock USDC: 5.000000 USDC per LPT

stand_ins.value: anvil, chain id 474747, one block a second; every key is a throwaway key made by the run
An ERC-20 with six decimals that anyone may mint (contracts/src/money/MockUSDC.sol)
The node prices in wei of the chain's native token. With 1,000,000 of its units to the dollar, one unit is one micro-USDC, so 1 USDC = 1 USD and the node's amounts are micro-USDC

Win probability 2^256 - 2, the largest the node accepts, and a face of the job price + 1 micro-USDC (0.999999 USD = 999,999, so 1,000,000: one ticket of 1 USDC a job). Each job settles one ticket and overpays 1 micro-USDC

stand_ins.stand_in: The signer's ticket limits in micro-USDC
stand_ins.value: --max-ticket-ev 2000000 and --max-batch-ev 20000000, read as micro-USDC because of the fixed rate above
RoundLength = 50 blocks of the block number the node reads (R-18); a round lasts longer when nobody starts the next one
SmolLM2-135M-Instruct served by llama.cpp; its answers are not checked, and a settled ticket does not show the work was done

A throwaway key the run makes, fixed in Parameters at deployment as its one authority: it announces and withdraws with lp2-params, and a change counts from the announce round + 7. No contract has an owner key, and the Controller's names are fixed at deployment

stand_ins.for: A Uniswap v2 pool of USDC and LPT on a public chain
stand_ins.value: A port of the v2 pair's mint and swap paths with v2's fee, cumulative prices and revert texts, no owner, no protocol fee and no flash swaps (contracts/src/money/TestPool.sol), seeded with 500,000 mock USDC and 100,000 test LPT; the Buyback admits only a pool with its runtime code hash and this deployment's two tokens

Parameters holds burn 100 %, TWAP interval 3,600 s, slippage bound 1 %, a buy every round and the TestPool above until G announces a change; the burn share is fixed, and a new pool must be one the executor asked accepts (POOL_INVALID at the announce): for the Buyback, a pool with the TestPool's runtime code hash and this deployment's two tokens. The executor, group 10, is the Buyback until G announces another

stand_ins.for: An executor and pool of another design, wherever liquidity is (owner's instruction of 2026-11-23)
stand_ins.value: ./dev demo buyback deploys a second Buyback, pinned to the same TestPool code, and a second TestPool seeded as the first, and G moves the buyback to them by announcing group 10 and group 9; no other contract is redeployed. An executor of another design is shown only by a test-only contract in the contract tests

stand_ins.stand_in: Tickets signed and redeemed by the demo
stand_ins.value: ./dev demo buyback makes the network share by signing and redeeming winning tickets directly (the payments and rewards demos prove the node's path); ./dev demo full runs the buyback beside real node jobs

./dev demo buyback sets each block's time with anvil's evm_setNextBlockTimestamp and mines a round's blocks at once, so the buyback-walk case runs at its own times, offset by the start time it records; ./dev demo full moves time once, by one TWAP interval, so that the keeper's buy has an observation old enough
An ERC-20 with 18 decimals (contracts/src/money/TestLPT.sol) that only Claims, fixed at deployment, may mint
Created once by the token's constructor for the deployer, outside every round's issuance (R-09); holders are given LPT from it by transfer (the ledger case's grant_lpt), never by a mint
An address the run makes up and whose key nobody holds, fixed in Claims at deployment; it receives each round's treasury amount and what the validator division leaves
V1, V2 and V3, registered nodes that bond 3,000, 2,000 and 1,800 test LPT to themselves, opt in and are seated in ./dev demo full; they cast no vote, so nothing they do judges work
Scores seats at most 3 members, Parameters' validator set size at deployment, which G may change (R-25); the three validators of ./dev demo full fill the seats

stand_ins.for: Whoever starts rounds, mints each round's validator and treasury amounts, buys and pokes
stand_ins.value: A throwaway key: ./dev demo buyback starts rounds and makes the walk's pokes and buys with it at the walk's times, then runs lp2-keeper --once --parameters-address, which buys or pokes at the executor in force for the round only when its call would succeed, and then leaves lp2-keeper running while the buyback moves to a second executor; ./dev demo full runs lp2-keeper --parameters-address through the run. Anyone may do any of these (R-10, R-16, R-18), so a stopped keeper delays them and loses nothing
